text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER — Sev 2: multiple inference pool nodes in us-west2 toggling NotReady -> Ready. Impact: increased 502s and elevated latencies for hosted inference. links: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-4245 :eyes:
chao: I'm on it, taking lead. will triage node health and pod restarts.
sara: looking at k8s, nodes cycling: gpu-wn-09 and gpu-wn-10 showing NotReady ~every 30-90s.
alex: pods on those nodes show repeated restarts; I see serving-runtime container OOMKilled on a few.
mike: kubelet logs from gpu-wn-09 (tail):
```
May 03 22:14:01 gpu-wn-09 kubelet[2167]: E0503 22:14:01.123456    2167 eviction_manager.go:302] eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage
May 03 22:14:01 gpu-wn-09 systemd[1]: Stopping kubelet.service...
May 03 22:14:02 gpu-wn-09 systemd[1]: Started kubelet.service.
May 03 22:14:02 gpu-wn-09 kubelet[2167]: I0503 22:14:02.234567    2167 kubelet.go:185] warm-restart: kubelet restarted without full reboot
```
mike: looks like kubelet service is restarting repeatedly (warm-restart) rather than nodes rebooting.
chao: ok - let's cordon and drain affected nodes to stop noisy restarts causing flapping. will also switch traffic to fallback-small model to reduce memory footprint.
ops-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/kubelet-warm-restart — commands: `kubectl cordon <node>`, `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`, check driver via `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi`.
rami: I cordoned gpu-wn-09 and kicked drain:
```
$ kubectl cordon gpu-wn-09
node/gpu-wn-09 cordoned
$ kubectl drain gpu-wn-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=5m
node/gpu-wn-09 evicted 14 pods
```
alex: sample pod describe shows OOMKilled reason:
```
State:          Terminated
  Reason:       OOMKilled
  Exit Code:    137
  Last State:   Terminated
  Message:      Killed process 12345 (serving-runtime) total-vm: 72Gi
```
chao: this matches a recent config change (yesterday) that bumped max_seq and increased KV cache size. Suggest routing realtime traffic to `model-35-small` while we stabilize. sara, can you flip the route?
sara: flipping route now -> updating traffic rule to fallback model for affected customer cohorts. will post verification.
ops-bot: traffic-routes update: /api/routes/serve/attach applied by sara.
ops-bot: healthcheck: `curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood-inference/health?model=fallback | head -n 1` -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
mike: good. scaling standby pool to absorb load: `kubectl scale deploy/serving-runtime-standby --replicas=8`
rami: pods moved off gpu-wn-09 onto other nodes, but we're seeing higher mem/GPU pressure cluster-wide. p50 latency up 120ms->250ms, error rate to ~4.8% (was 0.2%). partial customer impact on small set of high-QPS customers.
chao: @talia (infra) can you check GPU driver and kernel logs on gpu-wn-09/10? I suspect driver resets leading to kubelet restart loop.
talia: joining. grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi from gpu-wn-09.
talia: dmesg snippet: 
```
[May 03 22:13:59] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[May 03 22:13:59] kernel: Killed process 12345 (serving-runtime) total-vm: 73400320kB, anon-rss: 72800000kB
[May 03 22:14:00] nvidia: GPU reset: GPU HDA triggered reset
```
talia: driver reports GPU fault and a reset; this correlates with serving-runtime OOMs and kubelet restart attempts. I'll attempt a driver reload and a kubelet warm-restart first to avoid full node reprovision.
talia: running `ssh root@gpu-wn-09 'sudo systemctl restart kubelet'` and reloading nvidia modules now.
talia: kubelet restart output: `Job for kubelet.service restarted successfully`. watching for flapping.
mike: after restart, node enters Ready and remains stable so far. monitoring metrics.
chao: nice. keep traffic on fallback for 10 more minutes, then can gradually shift back if metrics look healthy.
rami: rolling back the model config that bumped max_seq is in progress (revert PR merged); will monitor for new OOMs.
alia: (ops-bot?) small typo, not relevant.
chao: action items: 1) add guardrail in model-onboarding to cap max KV cache *and* surface a diff warning. 2) add alert for >2 kubelet restarts per 5m per node. 3) create a short-term rule to auto-shift heavy models off nodes with repeated driver resets. 4) runbook update to include driver reload before full reprovision.
ops-bot: Incident timeline posted to https://incidents.redwood/4245/postmortem-draft — please add notes.
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied, traffic routed to fallback model, affected nodes cordoned/drained, driver reload and kubelet restart performed. Status: monitoring (SLA impact: minor, subset customers).
chao: closing handoff — we'll keep monitoring for 60m. if stable, mark resolved and schedule postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — root cause: GPU driver fault + memory pressure triggered by recent model config change; remediation: driver reload, kubelet warm-restart, routing rollback, config guardrails.
